result.markdown: --- title: >- [Table.to_csv()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Write the table's unformatted values to a CSV file. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package/blob/main/tinytab/_table.py#L215-L246){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Table.to_csv(path) ``` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [path]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The file to write. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Save a table, then read it back with `Table.from_csv()`: ::: {#dc428c7e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pathlib import Path from tinytab import Table path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "menu.csv" Table({"item": ["coffee", "bagel"], "price": [3.5, 2.25]}).to_csv(path) print(path.read_text()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` item,price coffee,3.5 bagel,2.25 ``` ::: :::
